package_info.why_malicious: The report is a high-level industry analysis and does not describe any specific malicious package or code. It discusses the rise of malicious open source packages and supply chain attacks in general, but does not provide concrete examples, code snippets, or package metadata for any particular malware.

behavioral_signatures: Malicious code embedded in open source packages
Malware that executes during build, install, or runtime phases
Packages that exfiltrate secrets or credentials
Packages that blend into legitimate development workflows
file_indicators: Unexpected scripts in package install or build files (e.g., setup.py, package.json, .github/workflows)
Unusual or obfuscated code in dependency files
network_indicators: Outbound network requests to unknown or suspicious domains during package installation or build
Connections to known malware command-and-control infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected or unauthorized code execution during package installation, build, or runtime. Use automated tools to scan dependencies for known malicious patterns, suspicious network activity, and unexpected file modifications. Employ Software Composition Analysis (SCA) and maintain a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) to track and vet all open source components. Continuously monitor for new vulnerability advisories and update dependencies promptly.
